Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corporation Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corporation's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are David Chen, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Harper, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Rodriguez, Chief Operating Officer; Tom Ellis, VP of Exploration; Karen Lee, VP of Marketing; Elena Vasquez, Chief Sustainability Officer; and Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to David Chen.

David Chen: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corporation delivered solid results in Q3 2024, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved record production volumes and meaningful progress on cost efficiencies across our portfolio. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on exploration successes and midstream expansions. We are focused on advancing high-return drilling in the Permian while optimizing our capital allocation. Further, we are working on sustainability enhancements and technology deployments to drive long-term value. We continue to adjust to market dynamics with disciplined hedging. We are advancing our debt reduction targets. We are evaluating bolt-on opportunities in core basins. Finally, we are taking steps to enhance shareholder returns through dividends and buybacks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Harper to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Lisa Harper: Thank you, David. As David mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $3.2 billion, up 28% year-over-year. Operating income was $1.6 billion, and net income was $1.1 billion. We generated $1.4 billion in free cash flow and returned $700 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $9.8 billion in debt and $2.2 billion in cash.

Good afternoon, everyone—though it's morning here—thank you for joining our Q3 2024 earnings call. I'll dive right into our EBITDA performance, which was a standout quarter, reflecting the strength of our portfolio and the execution of our multi-basin strategy. For the quarter, we reported adjusted EBITDA of $2.45 billion, representing a robust 32% year-over-year increase from $1.86 billion in Q3 2023. On a trailing twelve-month basis, EBITDA now stands at $9.8 billion, up 28% YoY. Let me walk you through the key drivers using our standard EBITDA bridge, which we've included in the earnings supplement on page 14.

Starting with volumes: Our total company-wide production averaged 465 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day, or MBOE/d, up 12% from 415 MBOE/d last year. Oil volumes specifically grew 15% to 320 Mbopd, driven primarily by our Permian Basin assets, where we brought online 28 new horizontal wells in the Delaware sub-basin. These Second Banana wells featured extended laterals averaging 12,500 feet, with enhanced fracs using 3,500 pounds of proppant per foot and ceramic diverters—resulting in initial production rates exceeding 2,400 BOE/d per well, 20% above our type curve. In the Eagle Ford, we maintained steady output at 85 Mbopd through disciplined D&C—drill and complete—cadence, offsetting natural declines.

This volume growth contributed about $280 million to the YoY EBITDA uplift. However, we did face some headwinds in the Gulf of Mexico offshore, where Hurricane Francine caused seven days of unplanned downtime at our Lobster field, shaving off roughly 5 MBOE/d for the month. We've since ramped back to full rates and are leveraging our subsea tie-backs to Chevron's Anchor FPSO for faster recovery.

Shifting to pricing: Realized oil prices strengthened to $68.50 per barrel, up from $52.10 in Q3 '23, benefiting from Brent averaging $81/bbl amid tighter OPEC+ cuts and resilient global demand from Asia. Our NYMEX WTI realization was $67.20, with differentials narrowing to $1.10/bbl thanks to improved Permian takeaway capacity post-Matterhorn Express pipeline startup. Natural gas prices held firm at $3.25 per Mcf, supported by strong LNG export demand to Europe, where our Haynesville assets realized a 15% premium to Henry Hub. Overall, this price tailwind added $520 million to EBITDA YoY, net of our 45% hedge position at a $65 WTI floor—our hedges locked in solid protection while allowing substantial upside capture.

On the cost side, we continue to deliver industry-leading efficiencies. Lease operating expenses, or LOE, dropped 18% to $7.80 per BOE from $9.50, driven by our digital oilfield initiatives, including AI-optimized pumpjack automation across 70% of our Permian legacy verticals, which reduced energy consumption by 22% and downtime by 15%. General and administrative costs as a percentage of revenue fell to 4.2% from 5.1%, reflecting headcount optimization post our Q1 divestiture of non-core DJ Basin assets to Occidental for $450 million. Transportation and gathering expenses were flat at $4.20/BOE, as we shifted more volumes to lower-cost TRP Park pipelines in the Permian.

These opex improvements generated $210 million of EBITDA accretion. Additionally, our midstream segment contributed $150 million, up 25% YoY, from higher throughput on our Eagle Ford NGL fractionation JV with Enterprise Products Partners, where fractionation margins expanded to $0.18/gallon on ethane rejection plays tied to winter demand.

A couple of strategic notes: Upstream EBITDA was $2.25 billion, or 92% of total, underscoring our focus on high-margin crude oil. We're allocating 65% of our $1.8 billion capex guidance to the Permian, targeting 15% inventory growth through seismic reprocessing and our first hybrid CO2-EOR pilot in the Wolfcamp C, which early data shows boosting recoveries by 12% at incremental costs under $20/BOE. Internationally, our North Sea Buzzard field with Suncor maintained flat production at 40 Mbopd, but UK ETS carbon pricing pressures are prompting accelerated electrification of platforms—we've hedged 80% of our '25 Scope 1 emissions exposure.

Looking ahead, we see sustained tailwinds from global oil demand projected at 103 MMb/d by IEA, despite macro volatility. Risks include potential WTI weakness to $65 if China growth slows below 4.5%, but our hedge book and cost outperformance position us for $10 billion-plus EBITDA in 2025 at $70 WTI. Free cash flow yield remains north of 12%, funding our $3 billion share repurchase authorization and 15% dividend hike announced today.

As we wrap up the financial overview with WTI averaging $82 per barrel and Brent at $86, driven by sustained OPEC+ production cuts and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, I'd like to dive into our balance sheet strength—specifically our debt levels, net debt position, and leverage ratios. Our disciplined capital allocation has continued to deliver meaningful deleveraging, positioning us exceptionally well for the volatility we all know characterizes our industry.

Total long-term debt stood at $9.8 billion as of September 30, 2024, down from $10.5 billion at year-end 2023 and a sharp reduction from the $12.2 billion peak in Q4 2022 following our transformative acquisition of the Eagle Ford assets from a peer amid the post-COVID consolidation wave. This represents a 21% year-over-year decline, primarily driven by $1.4 billion in debt repayments funded by robust free cash flow generation—$1.8 billion in Q3 alone, exceeding our guidance thanks to Permian Basin drilling efficiencies and Gulf of Mexico uptime above 98%.

Breaking it down by instrument: Our $3.0 billion revolving credit facility, with commitments from 20 banks led by JPMorgan and Wells Fargo, remains fully undrawn, providing ample liquidity headroom of $2.9 billion after letters of credit. Term loans total $2.5 billion, refinanced earlier this year at a blended SOFR-plus-175 basis points, shaving 50 basis points off our prior all-in cost. The balance, $4.3 billion, is in fixed-rate senior unsecured notes—maturities staggered through 2034, with our most recent $750 million 5.125% notes due 2031 issued in February at a yield below 5%, locking in low rates ahead of the Fed's anticipated pause on cuts. No near-term maturities pressure us, with the nearest at $500 million in 2026, which we plan to pre-fund via cash flow.

Shifting to net debt: We calculate this as total debt less cash and short-term investments. At quarter-end, net debt was $7.6 billion, reflecting $2.2 billion in cash equivalents and marketable securities. This marks a 24% reduction from $10.0 billion at the end of 2023, and we're now at our lowest net debt level since before the 2020 downturn. Key drivers include $850 million in non-core asset divestitures—primarily shallow-water Gulf of Mexico legacy fields sold to a mid-tier operator—and aggressive working capital management, capturing $300 million in receivables from our LNG-linked offtake contracts in Appalachia. Regionally, our Permian position, now 55% of production post-drillbit consolidation, generated 65% of this free cash flow, benefiting from D&C costs down 15% YoY to $550 per lateral foot thanks to our optimized cube frac designs and long-lateral laterals averaging 12,000 feet.

Leverage ratios—our north star metric for capital markets. Our net debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA stands at 1.6x, down from 2.4x at year-end 2023 and well below our long-term target of 1.5x-2.0x. For context, LTM Adjusted EBITDA hit $4.7 billion, boosted by Q3's $1.3 billion result—our strongest ever—fueled by 8% production growth to 650,000 boe/d and upstream margins of $52/boe amid low breakevens averaging $42/boe in the Permian. Gross debt to EBITDA is 2.1x, and debt-to-capitalization sits at 28%, firmly investment-grade territory akin to peers like ConocoPhillips or EOG Resources.

Our covenant compliance is rock-solid: 3.7x EBITDA interest coverage, with headroom exceeding 50% on all incurrence and maintenance tests under our credit agreement. Compared to the sector, where leveraged peers like Occidental hover around 2.5x amid their Anadarko integration, we're in the lower quartile, reflecting our shareholder-friendly framework—no dividends until 1.0x leverage, but now accelerating buybacks with $500 million authorized this quarter.

Strategically, this deleveraging unlocks optionality. We've hedged 65% of 2025 oil production at $75/bbl floors via collars and fixed swaps, insulating cash flow against a $70 WTI downside while preserving upside to Brent's $90+ potential on Red Sea disruptions. Technologically, our Permian AI-driven completions—partnering with Halliburton on PropX modeling—have cut cycle times 20%, directly feeding debt paydown. Internationally, our North Sea JVs with Equinor remain low-leverage at 0.8x asset-level, with Troll Phase III ramping FID next year.

Looking forward, we guide to $2.0-2.5 billion in 2024 free cash flow at strip prices, targeting net debt below $6.5 billion by year-end—pushing leverage to 1.3x. This sets the stage for 5-7% dividend growth in 2025 and M&A firepower in high-return basins like the DJ and Uinta, where we've penciled IRRs north of 30% at current gas prices.

I'll now turn to our lifting costs per BOE, a key lever for value creation in a volatile WTI environment, where we've seen Brent averaging just $82 per barrel YTD amid OPEC+ cuts and rising non-OPEC supply from the Permian. Lifting costs represent our direct operating expenses to produce and lift one barrel of oil equivalent from our producing assets—covering lease operating expenses like pumping, compression, water handling, maintenance, and labor, but excluding G&A, exploration, or DD&A. This metric is a cornerstone of our low-cost operator strategy.

In Q3 2024, our company-wide lifting costs came in at $11.85 per BOE, a 12% sequential improvement from $13.45 in Q2 and a robust 22% year-over-year decline from $15.20 in Q3 2023. For the full year to date, we averaged $12.60 per BOE, down 18% from last year and marking our lowest annual figure in recent history. Looking back five years, we've shaved costs from $17.80 per BOE in 2019—when Waha gas prices were negative and COVID shut-ins hit—to today's levels, representing a compounded annual reduction of about 7.5%.

Regionally, our flagship Permian Basin assets, which accounted for 68% of production, drove the outperformance. Permian lifting costs averaged $9.20 per BOE, down from $10.80 YoY, thanks to scale efficiencies in the Delaware and Midland sub-basins. This puts us in the top quartile versus peers—Pioneer Natural Resources reported $8.50 last quarter, while Occidental's blended Permian is around $10. Our Eagle Ford assets held steady at $13.50 per BOE, resilient despite higher water cut challenges from mature horizontals. Offshore Gulf of Mexico saw $22.40 per BOE—elevated due to subsea tie-backs and hurricane-related deferrals—but even here, we're 15% below prior-year levels post our Alaminos Canyon optimizations.

Our 2024 cost-out program has delivered $285 million in savings, or about $4.50 per BOE. We've bucketed these into technology deployment, operational standardization, and supply chain rigor. First, digital and automation tech: We've rolled out AI-driven predictive maintenance across 85% of our Permian pads using Halliburton's DecisionSpace 365 platform, integrated with our proprietary SCADA system. This has cut unplanned downtime by 28%, translating to $1.20 per BOE savings via fewer workovers. In the Eagle Ford, drone-based lease inspections and IoT sensors on ESPs reduced labor hours by 22%. Offshore, we're piloting unmanned platforms on our Holstein field revival, aiming to drop GoM costs to $18 per BOE by 2025.

Second, production enhancement: In the Permian, we've optimized frac designs with 4,500-foot laterals and 40 lb/ft proppant intensity, lowering pump times—our average frac cost per stage fell 11% to $25,000. Water management hit 72% recycling rate via our JV with Solaris, saving $450,000 per pad. Eagle Ford chemical initiatives stabilized water cuts, preserving LOE.

Third, supply chain: Inflation in steel and diesel was offset by multi-year deals with NOV and Schlumberger for 5-7% discounts. Vendor consolidation yielded another $0.80 per BOE. We also divested marginal vertical wells, improving portfolio average.

These efforts position us for margin resilience—at $70 WTI, Permian breakevens sub-$25 full-cycle. We're targeting sub-$11 company-wide by end-2024 via central facilities and AI modeling.

Now, on capital expenditure guidance, where we outline future spending plans and expected returns that underpin our disciplined allocation strategy. We remain laser-focused on delivering superior shareholder returns through high-return inventory, operational excellence, and prudent stewardship.

For 2024, we're guiding CapEx to $2.8 billion, about 45% of projected cash flow from operations at $75 WTI. This is a slight uptick from $2.6 billion in 2023, driven by accelerated Permian development. Multi-year: $3.0 billion in 2025, $3.2 billion in 2026, scaling with production toward 450-500k BOE/d by 2026—a CAGR below production growth, showing efficiency.

Upstream development 75%, or $2.1 billion: $1.4 billion for Permian D&C, running 14 rigs, 22 frac crews. Optimized cycle times under 200 days with "ApexFlow" design yielding 20-25% better EURs. Maintenance $420 million, tech $280 million including rig electrification slashing costs $150k/well. Exploration $280 million.

Permian 65% or $1.8 billion, targeting 3,200 locations sub-$40 breakevens. Eagle Ford 20%, Guyana 10% with Stabroek appraisal, North Sea infill.

Expected returns: Blended 22% IRR, 14-month payback at $75 WTI. Permian Delaware IPs 1,800 BOE/d, resilient to $60 WTI. Divested non-core, boosting FCF yield 12-15%. Digital "DrillOptix" cuts NPT 30%.

Risk-adjusted, 10+ years inventory, funding dividend up 10% to $2.20/share, buybacks, M&A.

I'll now turn the call over to Mike Rodriguez for an operational update.

Mike Rodriguez: Thank you, Lisa. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 465 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought the Second Banana pad online in the Permian Delaware, expected to contribute significantly to growth. We're also making progress on cost reductions.

To elaborate further, our total production averaged 278,000 BOE/d in the quarter—wait, scaling to our full metrics, it hit 465k BOE/d overall, up 9% QoQ from prior and 14% YoY. Oil at 320,000 bbl/d or 73% mix, up 11% QoQ and 17% YoY, powered by Permian Delaware with 28 new wells on 12,000-ft laterals delivering 1,800 BOE/d IPs. Eagle Ford steady. Gas at 468 MMcf/d or 78k BOE/d equiv, flat QoQ but up 5% YoY from Permian Black Shale.

Permian 68% at 189k BOE/d up 12% QoQ, Eagle Ford 52k, GoM 37k. Hedged 65% Q4 oil at $78. Guide Q4 285-295k total.

Now I will turn it over to Tom Ellis for an update on our exploration activities.

Tom Ellis: Thank you, Mike. We are excited about the potential of our exploration program. We recently completed a successful seismic survey in the Permian Basin and are planning to drill 28 exploration wells in the next year. We believe these wells have the potential to add significant reserves to our portfolio.

Good morning, everyone—I'll turn to our exploration and drilling activity updates, executing with discipline amid $80 WTI. Spudded 28 wells, 22 online at 98% success, IP30 1,450 Boe/d up 12% QoQ, EUR 1.1 MMboe, 72% oil.

Permian Delaware "Wolfcamp A-BC" 4-well pad 2,100 Boe/d IP (85% oil), 12k ft laterals, costs $850/ft, added 45 locations to 1,200. Midland Wolfcamp C-D 1,800 Boe/d. Eagle Ford "Eagle Ridge 7H" 1,100 Boe/d, costs $7.2M/well. DJ pilots 800 Boe/d, North Sea sidetracks 5k net.

Tech: "Apex Completion Lab" optimizes spacing, electric fracs cut emissions. Future: 3 rigs Q4, 110 completions, $450M D&C, high-grade 1,400 locations, eyeing M&A.

Finally, I'll turn it over to Karen Lee to discuss our marketing strategy.

Karen Lee: Thank you, Tom. We are focused on optimizing our marketing strategy to maximize the value of our production. We are seeing strong demand for our crude blends in the Gulf Coast market, and we are working to expand our customer base and strengthen relationships with existing customers. The impact on realizations from narrowed differentials is significant.

I will now turn it over to Elena Vasquez to discuss our sustainability efforts.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Karen. We are committed to reducing our environmental footprint and operating in a sustainable manner. We have made significant progress on reducing our greenhouse gas emissions and are investing in renewable energy projects. We are also working to improve our water management practices and protect biodiversity.

Thank you for the introduction—before we move further, I'd like to provide a detailed update on our environmental performance, specifically around spills, incidents, and remediation efforts. At Apex, environmental stewardship is core to our license to operate, ESG commitments, and long-term value creation. We're proud to report another strong quarter, outperforming benchmarks from ExxonMobil and Chevron per API's index.

Headline: Zero Tier 1 or Tier 2 spills—high-volume over 50-barrel threshold—our 11th consecutive quarter since Q1 2022. Total reportable spill volume 1.2 barrels, 72% YoY reduction from 4.3, below 2-barrel target. Incident frequency 0.04 per million hours vs. industry 0.12.

Upstream: Permian zero spills amid 8% rig count rise. GoM one 0.8-barrel hydraulic release contained via ROV, remediated in 24 hours no impact. Midstream 0.4 barrels pinhole, downstream zero. North Sea JV incident-free, LNG 100% uptime.

Remediation: $450k costs down 15% YoY. GoM 99.8% recovery with sorbents, bioremediation to <1 ppm verified by ERM. DJ chemical oxidants to TPH baseline, 98.7% YTD success vs. 92% industry.

Proactive: Apex Sentinel AI with SLB/Palantir covers 95% assets, 50k IoT sensors predict issues 92% accuracy. Drones surveyed 1,200 km Permian averting spills, acoustic testing pilots.

Financial upside: Costs 0.02% opex vs. 0.08% avg, 5% insurance discount, expedited permits, 15% flared gas capture to 98%, $75M 2025 capex for DAS, 90% water recycle saving 25M bbls freshwater.

This de-risks our $10B base amid $75-80 WTI, SEC rules. We're setting the standard.

I will now turn the call over to Raj Patel to discuss our technology initiatives.

Raj Patel: Thank you, Elena. We are leveraging technology to improve operational efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance safety. We are investing in automation, data analytics, and artificial intelligence to optimize our operations—such as our DrillOptix platform cutting NPT by 30%. We are also exploring new technologies such as carbon capture and storage to support net-zero goals and unlock EOR potential.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Energy Capital Partners. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on production volumes, total, oil, gas—QoQ and YoY changes?

David Chen: Thanks, John. Happy to dive into our production volumes here in Q3. We're laser-focused on high-margin barrels across Permian, Eagle Ford, and GoM. Total production averaged 465k BOE/d, up 12% YoY from 415k, strongest growth in years on new wells, productivity, 98.5% reliability.

Oil 320 Mbopd (73%), up 15% YoY, from Permian Delaware 28 wells 12k-ft laterals 1,800 BOE/d IP30 25% above type curve, EUR 1.2 MMboe. Eagle Ford 65% cuts. Gas 468 MMcf/d or 78k BOE/d, up 5% YoY from Permian yields, realized $3.25/Mcf premium.

Permian 68% 315k up 12%, Eagle Ford steady, GoM offset hurricanes. 65% hedged Q4 at $78 oil. Q4 guide 475-485k. Positions us for $450M FCF.

Operator: Our next question comes from Amy Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Amy Chen: Good morning. What are your expectations for EBITDA drivers next quarter?

Lisa Harper: Good morning, Amy. We expect continued volume growth from Permian, pricing stability with hedges, and opex efficiencies adding $200M+ tailwind. Guide $2.6-2.7B adjusted EBITDA Q4 at strip.

Operator: Our next question comes from Brian Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Brian Patel: Could you please provide more color on lifting costs trends?

Mike Rodriguez: Thanks, Brian. Q4 lifting sub-$11/BOE targeted, Permian $8.50 via AI maintenance, water recycle 75%, supply chain locks. Full-year savings $300M+.

Operator: Our next question comes from Laura Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Laura Kim: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

Tom Ellis: Great question, Laura. Strong IPs and de-risked 1,200+ Permian locations reinforce Permian focus 65% capex, accelerating to 3 rigs Q4, adding inventory for 15% ROCE. Opens M&A in stacks.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mark Ruiz with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mark Ruiz: What is the outlook for the new product in the coming years? [Referring to Permian crude blends]

Karen Lee: Thanks, Mark. Strong Gulf Coast demand for our low-sulfur blends, expanding to Asia via LNG offtakes, 10% volume growth 2025, lifting realizations $2/bbl.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sophia Grant with BlackRock. Please go ahead.

Sophia Grant: Could you elaborate on your sustainability targets?

Elena Vasquez: Absolutely, Sophia. Net-zero 2050 on track, 98% flare capture, emissions down 20% YoY via electrification, $75M capex for leak detection, water 90% recycle. Top-quartile per API.

Operator: Our next question comes from Derek Wong with Citadel. Please go ahead.

Derek Wong: What are the key technology initiatives you are focused on?

Raj Patel: Derek, key ones: AI completions with Halliburton reducing costs 20%, electric fracs 70% pads, CCS pilots in Permian for 12% recovery boost, digital twins for 30% NPT cut.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to David Chen for closing remarks.

David Chen: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
